site_selection_index_test: Images were acquired from clinically suspicious oral lesions identified after clinical examination, and also from a clinically healthy-appearing area on the corresponding contralateral anatomical side.
technique: A multispectral autofluorescence endoscope using 355 nm pulsed laser excitation acquired tissue autofluorescence emission at 390 ± 20 nm, 452 ± 22.5 nm, and >500 nm bands with a 10 mm circular field of view and <3 s acquisition time per multispectral image. Images were acquired from the suspicious lesion and contralateral healthy-appearing mucosa, then preprocessed, converted to autofluorescence intensity feature maps, and classified using L1-SVM models with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation.
positivity_threshold: Validation samples were classified as cancer/precancer when the predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to an optimized threshold selected from the training-set ROC curve; otherwise they were classified as benign.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level score ≥ optimized cancer/precancer threshold
comments_index_test: Index-test performance was estimated internally using leave-one-patient-out cross-validation of a machine-learning classifier; no external validation cohort was reported. The VELscope comparison was simulated rather than performed with an actual VELscope device.

index_test_arm_label: single-feature L1-SVM model mimicking the VELscope
index_test_reagent_name: single-feature L1-SVM model mimicking the VELscope
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious oral lesions were imaged; a clinically healthy-appearing area on the corresponding contralateral anatomical side was also imaged during the acquisition protocol.
technique: A multispectral autofluorescence endoscopic image was acquired in vivo, then a linear L1-SVM model using one feature—the combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm—was trained and cross-validated with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation to simulate VELscope emission. Image-level scores were classified as cancer/precancer if greater than or equal to the optimized threshold and benign otherwise.
positivity_threshold: Validation samples were classified as cancer/precancer if the predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold; otherwise they were classified as benign.
comments_index_test: This was not an actual VELscope device examination; it was a computational single-feature L1-SVM model designed to simulate VELscope autofluorescence emission using the same multispectral autofluorescence image dataset as the main model, so this arm is not independent of the multispectral arm.

site_selection_index_test: The smear was taken from the clinically malignant or potentially malignant oral cavity lesion, using the cytobrush all over the lesion.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was collected before biopsy using a cytobrush all over the lesion and stored in PreservCyt Thinprep.
technique: A cytobrush smear was taken all over the oral lesion before biopsy and stored in PreservCyt Thinprep. Three cytologic slides were prepared from each lesion sample using a Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge, stained by Papanicolaou, and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al.
positivity_threshold: Cytology was considered positive when classified as high-risk: high-grade lesions, suspicious for malignancy, or squamous cell carcinoma.
calibration_of_assessors: Two cytologists independently performed cytologic analyses, compared their results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist.
comments_index_test: Cytology, DNA-ICM, and combined analyses were performed on overlapping specimens/patients; DNA ploidy was measured on the same slide after cytology. Ten cytology samples were inadequate, leaving 88 cytology cases analyzed.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically malignant or potentially malignant oral cavity mucosal lesions were sampled; one smear was taken from each patient using a cytobrush all over the lesion before biopsy.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear per patient was collected before biopsy using a cytobrush over the entire lesion and stored in PreservCyt Thinprep.
technique: Cytologic slides were uncovered in xylene and stained by the Feulgen-Schiff method. DNA ploidy was measured with the semi-automated MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station. Individual nuclei with definable boundaries were selected; at least 35 normal oral epithelial cell nuclei were used for calibration, integrated optical density values were converted to 2c reference values, coefficient of variation of reference cells <5% was required, and after calibration at least 200 nuclei per slide were randomly selected, with suspicious nuclei also included. Results were analyzed using MotiCyte software and classified as euploid or aneuploid.
positivity_threshold: The sample was considered aneuploid if a stemline DNA index was <0.90 and >1.10 or <1.80 and >2.20 or <3.60 and >4.40, or if there were cells exceeding 9c content; otherwise it was considered euploid.
comments_index_test: DNA-ICM was performed on the same cytologic specimen/slide used for brush cytology; 15 DNA-ICM samples were inadequate and 83 cases were evaluated for DNA ploidy.

site_selection_index_test: A smear was taken from the clinically malignant or potentially malignant oral cavity lesion, using a cytobrush all over the lesion.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was collected before biopsy using a cytobrush over the entire lesion and stored in PreservCyt ThinPrep.
technique: Three cytologic slides were prepared from each lesion sample using a semi-automated cytocentrifuge. Cytology slides were Papanicolaou-stained and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al. For DNA-ICM, slides were uncovered in xylene, Feulgen-Schiff stained, and analyzed with a semi-automated DNA cytometer. At least 35 normal oral epithelial nuclei were used for calibration, coefficient of variation of reference cells <5% was required, then at least 200 nuclei per slide were randomly selected, with morphologically suspicious nuclei also included. Results were classified as euploid or aneuploid and combined with cytology results.
positivity_threshold: Combined positive appears to require both methods positive: cytologic high-risk result and DNA-ICM aneuploid result. Cytologic high-risk results were defined as high-grade lesions, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC; DNA-ICM aneuploidy was defined by abnormal stemline DNA index thresholds or cells exceeding 9c content.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: high-risk cytology and DNA aneuploidy
comments_index_test: Combined-arm analysis appears to include only cases where brush cytology and DNA-ICM were both negative or both positive, totaling 54, despite 98 patients receiving sampling. Inadequate and/or discordant results may have been excluded from combined diagnostic accuracy estimates, which could affect applicability and risk of bias.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to the clinically visible oral lesion; biopsy was taken from stained sites, and in non-stained lesions the biopsy site was decided clinically.
technique: Patients rinsed the mouth with water, then used 1% acetic acid mouthwash for 20 seconds. Then 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a cotton swab, followed by acetic acid mouthwash to remove excess stain; staining was then recorded as positive or negative regardless of intensity.
positivity_threshold: The staining was recorded as positive or negative irrespective of the intensity of the stain.
comments_index_test: NA

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied over the oral lesion, covering approximately a 2 cm margin all around the lesion; biopsy was then taken from the area stained maximum.
technique: 1% toluidine blue solution was prepared; the mouth was rinsed with water, followed by a 1% acetic acid rinse for 20 seconds, the area was dried with gauze, dye was gently applied with a cotton swab for 1 minute over the lesion and approximately 2 cm surrounding margin, then a 1% acetic acid rinse was given for 1 minute and dye uptake was observed under proper light/exposure. Excess stain was removed by gentle swabbing with 1% acetic acid.
positivity_threshold: A stain was considered positive for malignancy if the lesion diffusely or partly stained dark blue (royal or navy blue), or had a stippled appearance. All equivocal lesions were considered positively stained unless proved otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue or stippled stain retention
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was evaluated in a parallel Group B arm rather than paired within the same patients as Group A; allocation used alternate sampling, and the authors note no proper randomization was adopted.

site_selection_index_test: Patients with symptoms/signs suggestive of oral premalignant lesions or suspected oral malignancy underwent toluidine blue staining; identified oral/oropharyngeal lesions were the focus after comprehensive head and neck examination.
technique: Mouth rinsed with water for 20 seconds to remove debris, then 1% acetic acid applied for 20 seconds to remove ropey saliva, followed by 1% toluidine blue oral rinse for 20 seconds; 1% acetic acid rinse was repeated to remove mechanically retained stain, and finally the mouth was rinsed with water.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue; light staining or no color was considered negative.
comments_index_test: The paper inconsistently labels the toluidine blue concentration: methods describe a 1% modified toluidine blue/oral rinse, whereas the figure caption/bottle label states 0.1% solution. Analysis is patient-level; lesion-level denominators are not separately reported.

site_selection_index_test: Targeted application to clinically suspected oral PMD lesions: patients had white or red-and-white oral lesions suspicious of PMD, and 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion.
technique: Patients rinsed with clean water; lesions were dried with gauze and photographed; 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion using a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds; the lesion was photographed again and observed for colour change.
positivity_threshold: Positive if the lesion appeared opaque white/acetowhite; negative if the lesion showed no colour change.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The examiner was not blinded to clinical history/examination information, or at minimum had access to it: the principal investigator obtained detailed history and performed the clinical examination before applying the agents.
comments_index_test: Paired sequential design: the same 31 patients/lesions received acetic acid first, then toluidine blue, followed by biopsy. The authors also note that a single examiner performed all observations, so subjectivity/interobserver variation for acetic acid interpretation was not assessed.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to the clinically suspected oral PMD lesion; eligible lesions were white or red-and-white oral lesions suspicious of PMD.
technique: After acetic acid application, 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion using a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds, then decolorized with acetic acid, and the lesion was photographed.
positivity_threshold: The lesion was considered toluidine blue positive if it retained blue color after staining; lesions with no uptake or questionable uptake were considered negative.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Index-test examiner blinding to clinical information was not reported; the principal investigator obtained history and performed clinical examination before test application, suggesting clinical information was available, but the toluidine blue applicator/interpreter was not separately identified.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied sequentially after acetic acid in the same patients/lesions, so this arm is not independent of the acetic-acid arm and prior acetic-acid exposure may affect interpretation.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected OPMD lesions or non-healing ulcers; when a lesion was >2 cm, multiple TB electrospun fiber patches were placed adjacent to each other to cover the affected area.
technique: A cotton tip was used to apply 1% acetic acid to the lesion for 20 s, then a 2×2 cm electrospun fiber patch containing 2% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion for 20 s, and mechanically retained stain was removed by applying 1% acetic acid with a cotton tip for 20 s. Staining color/intensity was then measured by one oral medicine dentist.
positivity_threshold: Positive staining was defined as dark blue staining; pale or no staining was treated as negative.
comments_index_test: Lesion-level diagnostic accuracy analysis included 36 lesions in 30 patients, so some patients contributed more than one lesion. The authors note that this first study of TB-containing electrospun fibers did not compare the method with standard TB staining protocols.

site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush samples were collected from the suspicious oral lesion and from the contralateral normal side of the oral cavity in the same subject.
specimen_collection: Oral epithelial cells were collected non-invasively using a Rovers Orcellex cytobrush: after mouth rinse, the brush was applied with pressure to the suspicious lesion and turned 10 times, placed into PBS on ice, then the same procedure was performed on the contralateral normal site.
technique: Paired lesional and contralateral cytobrush samples were thawed, cells dislodged, centrifuged, lysed in RIPA buffer, and lysates assayed for hBD-2 and hBD-3 by ELISA. For proof-of-concept, discovery, and internal validation, sandwich ELISA with optimized Peprotech hBD-2/hBD-3 antibody pairs was used; for external validation, Phoenix Pharmaceuticals hBD-2 and hBD-3 ELISA kits were used per vendor instructions. Average OD values were blank-subtracted, hBD-3/hBD-2 ratios were calculated for lesion and contralateral sites, and BDI was calculated as the lesional ratio divided by the contralateral normal ratio.
positivity_threshold: BDI cutoff value of 1.25; a value at or above 1.25 was considered indicative of cancer/positive and would necessitate biopsy.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Index-test laboratory operators/investigators were blinded to pathology diagnoses until BDI scores were obtained.
comments_index_test: ELISA reagent source differed by cohort: proof-of-concept, discovery, and internal validation used Peprotech antibody-pair sandwich ELISA, while external validation studies used Phoenix Pharmaceuticals hBD-2/hBD-3 ELISA kits. Main analyzed cohort is reported as 92 subjects/lesions, although Table 1 values appear internally inconsistent with that total.

site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush samples were taken from OSCC lesional sites and corresponding contralateral normal sites; in healthy participants, samples were taken from left and right cheek or tongue.
specimen_collection: Specimens were collected non-invasively using a Rovers Orellex cytobrush. Participants rinsed with water; before biopsy, the clinician applied the brush to the mucosal surface of the suspicious lesion with pressure and turned the brush head 10 times, then placed it in PBS on ice. The same was done on the contralateral normal side. For MICA, samples were collected in PBS, added to EDTA vacutainer tubes, and processed within 2–3 hours.
technique: MICA used cytobrush-derived intact cells injected into lesion and contralateral microchannels under 40 mbar pressure until adequate cell density. Cells were fixed with 4% formaldehyde for 15 min, rinsed, blocked with BSA, permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100, incubated with DAPI plus fluorescent anti-hBD-3 and anti-hBD-2 antibodies for 1 h, washed, imaged, and analyzed by fluorescence intensity. BDI was calculated as [hBD-3 pixel/hBD-2 pixel] in the lesion divided by [hBD-3 pixel/hBD-2 pixel] in contralateral normal tissue.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: MICA-BDI was a proof-of-principle/point-of-care feasibility assay, not the main multi-center diagnostic accuracy validation. It compared 5 OSCC patients with 5 healthy participants and did not report a MICA-specific diagnostic cutoff; controls were healthy participants rather than patients with suspicious benign lesions.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious leukoplakia lesion areas were selected for staining; the stain was applied to suspicious areas rather than as a whole-mouth rinse.
technique: After clinical recording and photography, clinically suspicious lesion areas were treated with 1% acetic acid using a cotton bud for 20 seconds; this was repeated once and rinsed with water. Toluidine blue was then applied with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds. The lesion was decolorized with 2% acetic acid using a cotton bud for 20–30 seconds and photographed.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy; light blue retention was considered positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy; lesions without retention were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark or light blue stain retention
comments_index_test: NA

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered oral mucosa was selected after comprehensive clinical examination; TB staining was used to identify the biopsy site, with biopsy from the TB-positive region if staining was positive and from the clinical site if staining was negative.
technique: 1% toluidine blue was applied in four steps: rinse the oral cavity with water for 20 seconds to remove debris; apply or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 seconds; apply or rinse with 1% TB solution for 20 seconds; then apply or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 seconds to remove mechanically retained stain.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or navy blue stain was considered positive, even if only the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion was stained or stippled; light blue staining was considered doubtful, and no colour absorption was negative.
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons at the selected institutions were trained by an Oral Medicine expert, including live demonstrations of TB application to familiarize them with the procedure.
comments_index_test: Five patients received TB testing but lacked histopathological diagnosis, so accuracy calculations were based on 60 rather than 65 patients.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, photographed the lesions, and selected the lesion areas to be examined.
technique: The lesion was cleaned with a cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, toluidine blue was applied with a different cotton tip for 30 seconds, excess dye was removed using a third cotton bud soaked with 1% acetic acid, and the patient then rinsed the mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was the one which color changed to blue, while a negative lesion was with no change.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue diagnostic accuracy appears to include both the toluidine-blue-only group and patients who received both substances. There is a patient-count inconsistency: Methods state toluidine blue was applied to 33 patients and both substances to 24 patients, whereas Table 2 reports 67 specimens from 54 patients.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically selected suspected oral lesions; an oral medicine specialist recorded findings, photographed lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: A gauze soaked with vinegar was applied to a clean and dry lesion for one minute; the researcher then noted the changes and photographed the lesion.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white. When a lesion did not change or changed to transparent white, a negative finding was indicated.
comments_index_test: Diagnostic accuracy for acetic acid is reported at lesion/specimen level and includes 83 specimens from 57 patients; this may include patients/lesions from both the vinegar-only and combined vinegar plus toluidine-blue groups. Methods state 30 vinegar-only patients and 24 combined-test patients, which does not exactly match the 57 patients reported in Table 3.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist selected the lesion areas to be examined. For the combined arm, vinegar was applied first followed by toluidine blue; biopsy targeting depended on the staining pattern: the area that became both opaque white and blue was selected, both areas were biopsied if they were not coincident, and the central area was biopsied if no color change occurred.
technique: For the combined arm, vinegar was applied first, followed by toluidine blue. Vinegar was applied with gauze soaked in vinegar to a clean, dry lesion for one minute, after which changes were noted and the lesion photographed. Toluidine blue application involved cleaning the lesion with a cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, applying toluidine blue with a different cotton tip for 30 seconds, removing excess toluidine blue with a third cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, and then having the patient rinse the mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was indicated for a lesion with color changed to both opaque white and blue; a negative finding was a lesion not demonstrating these combined changes.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: opaque white change and blue stain
blinding_index_test_examiner: The examiner had access to clinical lesion findings and photographs when selecting areas to examine; no formal blinding to clinical information was reported.
comments_index_test: Combined-arm lesion/specimen count is slightly inconsistent: Results text says both reagents were applied to 27 lesions, but Table 4 reports 28 specimens from 24 patients and totals 28 specimens in the 2x2 table. Use 28 as the analyzed specimen-level denominator for diagnostic accuracy.

site_selection_index_test: Suspicious oral cavity lesions identified after detailed history and clinical examination were stained with toluidine blue; the biopsy site was selected on the basis of dye retention.
technique: After clinical examination, suspicious oral cavity lesions were stained with toluidine blue, and areas retaining dye were used to guide biopsy-site selection. The paper does not report detailed rinse/contact-time steps.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that showed dark blue staining were considered positive for premalignant or malignant tissue; light staining or no colour was considered negative.
comments_index_test: Both toluidine blue and NBI were administered to the same 44 patients, so index-test arms are paired/non-independent. Biopsy site selection was influenced by toluidine-blue and/or NBI findings, which may affect verification of test accuracy.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious oral cavity lesions were examined; patients underwent white-light endoscopy followed by NBI, and the suspected area was photographed.
technique: Patients first underwent zero-degree endoscopic examination under white light, followed by NBI examination of the oral cavity lesion; the suspected area was photographed. NBI was used to visualize mucosal vascular patterns, with superficial capillaries/IPCLs appearing as brown dots.
positivity_threshold: Altered or hypervascularity and increased capillaries/brown dots were considered suggestive of malignancy; uniform or normal vascularity was considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: altered vascularity with brown dots
comments_index_test: All 44 patients received both NBI and toluidine blue, so index-test arms are paired/non-independent. Biopsy site selection was influenced by the screening tests; if NBI and toluidine blue showed different areas, biopsies were taken from two sites.

site_selection_index_test: MB was applied directly to the clinically identified oral leukoplakia lesion/target area after clinical examination; all study lesions were on the buccal mucosa.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds, the target mucosa was dried with gauze, 1% MB dye was applied directly to the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds, then patients rinsed again with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to remove excess dye; stain retention intensity was then assessed.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered positive; wide, shallow, faint, pale royal blue stains or no retention were considered negative.
comments_index_test: MB-alone results are not independent from the double-staining arm: the same 50 patients were stained consecutively with MB followed by Lugol's iodine, and MB performance was analyzed from the first staining step.

site_selection_index_test: MB was applied to the target oral leukoplakia lesion, and LI was applied to lesional and perilesional sites; all study lesions were on the buccal mucosa.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds, the target mucosa was dried, MB was applied directly to the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds, patients rinsed again with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to remove excess dye, MB retention was assessed, and then 3% LI was applied to lesional and perilesional sites with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds.
positivity_threshold: Double-staining positive for dysplasia was based on absence of LI staining after MB/LI staining: pale yellow or unstained LI-negative areas were considered dysplastic; dark brown LI-positive areas were considered normal. MB dark royal/deep blue was considered positive MB retention, while pale/no MB retention was MB-negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: Lugol negative pale yellow or unstained area
comments_index_test: Same 50 patients underwent MB first and then LI; the double-staining arm is sequential and not independent of the MB-alone arm. There is also a concentration inconsistency: the abstract states 5% MB, whereas the Methods section describes MB dye as 1%.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically diagnosed OPMD lesions/oral tissues were examined; white light was first used to visualize the lesion extent, then violet light was used to examine suspicious lesions for loss of autofluorescence.
technique: Conventional oral examination was first performed under incandescent light, then room and operatory lights were dimmed. Oral tissue was examined with Identafi® white light to visualize lesion extent, then the device was switched to violet light to assess loss of autofluorescence; lesions displaying LOA were blanched to evaluate diascopic fluorescence.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed loss of autofluorescence were considered positive; lesions with no LOA or gain of autofluorescence were negative. On blanching, complete blanching was considered negative and partial blanching positive for LOA.
comments_index_test: Diagnostic accuracy was analyzed at lesion level; the same 63 lesions appear to have undergone both Identafi® violet light and green-amber light before toluidine blue, so index-test arms are not independent.

site_selection_index_test: Oral tissue/OPMD lesions were examined with Identafi®; the green-amber light was used to visualize differences in vasculature between normal and abnormal tissue.
technique: After conventional oral examination, room and operatory lights were dimmed. The lesion was first viewed with Identafi® white light, then violet light, and then the device was switched to green-amber light so the examiner could directly observe tissue vasculature/arrangement of blood vessels in abnormal tissue.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with diffuse vascularity that appeared darker under green-amber light were considered positive.
comments_index_test: Same 63 lesions appear to have undergone all index tests. Biopsy site selection incorporated Identafi® findings, toluidine blue staining, and clinical judgment, which may introduce incorporation/site-selection bias for diagnostic accuracy estimates.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to the lesion after Identafi screening; the paper describes that 'After screening with Identafi® lesion were stained with toluidine blue' and that the solution was 'applied to the lesion with cotton swab.'
technique: Patients rinsed with water for 20 seconds; 1% acetic acid was applied for 20 seconds; the area was dried with gauze; 1% toluidine blue solution was applied to the lesion with a cotton swab for 1 minute; 1% acetic acid was then applied for 1 minute; finally, patients rinsed with water again.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue stain uptake was considered positive. A light blue staining or absence of staining was taken as a negative.
comments_index_test: Same 49 patients/63 lesions underwent Identafi screening followed by toluidine blue staining; biopsy-site selection considered LOA, toluidine-blue-positive mucosa, and clinical judgment, so the index tests were sequential and applied to overlapping lesions rather than independent study arms.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected oral leukoplakia lesions/suspected lesions in the oral cavity.
technique: Participants first underwent allergy testing by skin scratch test; acetic acid solution was then applied to suspected lesions on the first day, with pre- and post-application images taken. Lesions staining positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to reduce false positives.
positivity_threshold: Acetowhite appearance after acetic acid application was treated as indicating dysplasia.
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesions, stain application, and post-staining assessment were standardized across all examiners.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Ambiguous: different examiners performed screening/recruitment and stain application to prevent bias, but the paper does not specify whether the acetic-acid examiner was blinded to patient history, clinical information, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: All three index tests appear to have been applied to the same patient cohort, with acetic acid and Lugol’s iodine on day 1 and toluidine blue on the following day; arm independence may therefore be limited. There is also a denominator inconsistency: 45 patients received acetic acid, but the acetic-acid 2x2 table totals 34 analyzed results.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected oral leukoplakia lesions.
technique: Lugol's iodine staining was applied to the suspected lesions on the first day, with pre- and post-application images taken; lesions staining positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to reduce false positives.
positivity_threshold: NR
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesions, stain application, and post-staining assessment were standardized across examiners.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners performed screening/recruitment and stain application to prevent bias, but the paper does not specify whether Lugol's iodine examiners were blinded to clinical history, demographics, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: Lugol's iodine protocol and positivity criterion are poorly described. There is also an apparent denominator inconsistency: the study reports 45 assessed subjects, but Table 2 Lugol's iodine diagnostic counts sum to 34.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to the clinically suspected oral leukoplakia lesions.
technique: After screening and clinical examination, patients underwent vital staining; toluidine blue staining was performed on the day after acetic acid and Lugol's iodine application. Pre- and post-staining images were taken, and lesions that stained positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to reduce false positives.
positivity_threshold: Positive staining with toluidine blue; no more detailed intensity or retention criterion was specified.
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesions, stain application, and post-staining assessment were standardized across examiners.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners performed screening/recruitment and stain application to prevent bias, but the paper does not specify whether the toluidine blue examiner was blinded to patient history, clinical information, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: All three index tests appear to have been applied to the same participants, so arms are not independent. There is also a denominator inconsistency: 45 subjects were reportedly assessed, but the toluidine blue TP/FN/FP/TN counts in Table 2 sum to 34.

site_selection_index_test: OLBC was applied to the patients' oral mucosal lesions before surgical biopsy; lesion sites included labial/buccal mucosa, lateral tongue, floor of mouth, and alveolar ridge/palate, but no detailed site-selection rule was reported.
specimen_collection: OLBC specimens were collected with an Orelcelx brush under local anesthesia before surgical biopsy; brush heads were immediately placed into methanol-based buffered preservative vials.
technique: OLBC was performed with the Orelcelx brush under local anesthesia before surgical biopsy. Brush heads were placed into ThinPrep PreservCyt preservative, transferred to the laboratory, processed into liquid-based cytology slides using the ThinPrep 2000 processor, Papanicolaou stained with ThinPrep reagents, and then assessed cytologically using the modified 2014 Bethesda system.
positivity_threshold: Cytology slides were classified into five modified Bethesda categories: atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, cyto OLP/OLL, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, and OSCC. For the OED/OSCC diagnostic comparison, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, and OSCC appear to constitute the positive cytology categories, although a binary positivity threshold is not explicitly stated.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytologic low-grade SIL or worse
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR; cytology slides were described as blindly assessed, but the paper does not explicitly state that assessors were blinded to the histopathology/reference standard result.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR; the paper reports blind cytology assessment but does not specify whether assessors were blinded to patient history, demographics, clinical appearance, or other clinical information.
comments_index_test: Initial OLBC cohort was 315 patients, but 31 samples were excluded for inadequate cellularity, leaving 284 analyzed. Binary positivity for OED/OSCC is not explicitly defined in methods and is inferred from reported Bethesda cytology categories and Table 2 diagnostic comparisons.

index_test_reagent_name: oral brush biopsy using Orelcex® brush
site_selection_index_test: Brush cytology was applied to clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia or oral squamous cell carcinoma lesions before surgical biopsy; no more detailed within-lesion site-selection procedure was reported.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy samples were collected using an Orelcex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy, then preserved in methanol-based ThinPrep® PreservCyt vials.
technique: Patients underwent oral brush biopsy with the Orelcex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy. Samples were preserved in ThinPrep® PreservCyt, transported to the laboratory, processed into liquid-based cytology slides using the ThinPrep® 2000 processor according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and Papanicolaou ThinPrep® slides were cytologically graded using the modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system.
positivity_threshold: No single binary positive/negative cutoff was stated. OLBC was graded using modified Bethesda categories: atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, or OSCC; proposed OLBC grading scores were 12 = no dysplasia, 9 = low-grade SIL, 6 = high-grade SIL, and 3 = OSCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytological low-grade SIL or worse
comments_index_test: One of 72 OLBC slides was excluded from OLBC grading analysis because of a Papanicolaou staining defect, so the analyzed denominator for this arm is 71. Detailed brush-site selection within lesions was not reported.

index_test_reagent_name: DNA mismatch repair proteins (MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2)
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples were obtained from clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia or OSCC lesions before surgical biopsy; lesion locations included lateral tongue, floor of mouth, labial/buccal mucosa, and alveolar ridge/palate, but no more detailed site-selection procedure was reported.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy samples were collected using an Orcellex/Orelcex brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy, preserved in ThinPrep PreservCyt vials, and remaining cells were processed into FFPE cell blocks.
technique: Remaining cells from ThinPrep oral brush cytology vials were processed into FFPE cell blocks using the thromboplastin-plasma method. Cell block adequacy was checked by H&E staining, with adequacy defined as at least 1 × 10^6 cells. Standard ICC staining was then performed on 4-μm sections for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2 using Agilent Dako antibodies. Staining was scored by intensity and percentage of positive cells; each protein’s index score was intensity score multiplied by positive-cell percentage score, and the cumulative score was the sum of the four protein index scores.
positivity_threshold: Cumulative index diagnostic cut-offs: 7.76–12 = no dysplasia; 5.51–7.75 = low-risk lesion; 2.76–5.5 = high-risk lesion; 0–2.75 = OSCC.
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR; the paper states that ICC slides were assessed blindly, but does not explicitly specify blinding to the histopathological reference standard.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR; nonspecific blinding is reported, but the paper does not state whether ICC assessors were blinded to clinical information such as patient history, demographics, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: The cumulative criteria arm used the same adequate OLBC-derived cell block samples as the other reported indices; 38 of 110 initially stained cell blocks were excluded for inadequate cellularity, leaving 72 cases for MMR ICC analysis.

index_test_reagent_name: cumulative MMR index and OLBC grading scores
site_selection_index_test: Brush cytology samples were taken from clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia or OSCC lesions before surgical biopsy; lesion sites included lateral tongue, floor of mouth, labial/buccal mucosa, and alveolar ridge/palate. No more detailed site-selection rule was reported.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy specimens were collected using an Orcellex/Orelcex brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy, preserved in ThinPrep PreservCyt vials, and processed into liquid-based cytology slides and FFPE cell blocks.
technique: Combined criteria were generated by preparing OLBC slides and FFPE cell blocks from brush samples, grading cytology using a modified Bethesda system, staining 4-μm cell block sections for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2, scoring staining intensity and percentage of positive cells, summing the four protein index scores as the cumulative MMR index, and combining this with OLBC grading scores to form the combined index.
positivity_threshold: Combined index score ranges were: 8.26–12 = no dysplasia; 5.76–8.25 = low-grade lesion; 3.76–5.75 = high-grade lesion; 0–3.75 = OSCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: low combined index score below no-dysplasia range
blinding_index_test_assessors: Slides were reported as assessed blindly by two independent observers, but the paper does not specify whether they were blinded to the histopathological reference standard.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The paper reports blinded slide assessment but does not specify whether observers were blinded to clinical information such as patient history, lesion appearance, demographics, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: Combined criteria appear to be derived within the same cohort using ROC/Youden-based cut-offs and were not externally validated. A substantial proportion of original cell blocks were excluded for inadequate cellularity, and one OLBC slide was excluded because of a Papanicolaou staining defect, which may affect applicability of the combined index.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions that were accessible for sampling were selected; inaccessible lesion sites were excluded.
specimen_collection: Material was collected from the oral cavity lesion using a commercially available toothbrush with medium bristles and deposited onto a glass slide.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure. For BR, a commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush was used to obtain material with minimal discomfort; the material was deposited on a glass slide. Smears were prepared and stained with H&E, PAP, and MGG; H&E and PAP smears were fixed in isopropyl alcohol and MGG smears were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Cytology results were categorized according to the oral Bethesda system as NILM, LSIL, HSIL, or SCC; the paper does not explicitly define a binary positivity threshold.
comments_index_test: All four cytology techniques were performed on each case, so index-test arms are paired/non-independent. BR cytology was performed in 27 cases, but diagnostic accuracy versus histopathology was based on the 23 cases with histopathological evaluation.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were sampled; lesions inaccessible for sampling were excluded.
specimen_collection: Material was collected from the oral lesion using a commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush as the modified brush cytology technique; this brush-collected material was then used for BRCC.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline. Material was obtained using a medium-bristle toothbrush. For BRCC, the brush-obtained material was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and cytocentrifuged using program No. 1 at 1250 rpm for 3 minutes. Smears were then prepared and stained with H&E, PAP, and MGG.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: All four cytology techniques were applied to the same 27 cases, so arms are paired/non-independent. Diagnostic accuracy for BRCC was based only on the 23 cases with available histopathology, not all 27 cytology cases.

index_test_reagent_name: commercially available plastic ice cream spoon
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; lesions inaccessible for sampling were excluded.
specimen_collection: Scrape cytology material was obtained from the oral lesion using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure. Modified scrape cytology was then performed using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon; smears were prepared for H&E, Papanicolaou, and MGG staining, with H&E/PAP smears fixed in isopropyl alcohol and MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Cytological diagnoses were categorized according to the oral Bethesda system as NILM, LSIL, HSIL, or SCC; a separate explicit binary positivity threshold was not stated.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC cytology
comments_index_test: Histopathology was available for only 23 of 27 cases, and for the SR arm a definitive cytology diagnosis was not offered in 2 histopathology cases; diagnostic accuracy calculations for SR were therefore based on 21 cases with an offered diagnosis.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were sampled; inaccessible lesions were excluded.
specimen_collection: Scrape cytology material was obtained using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline; scrape cytology material obtained using a plastic ice cream spoon was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 minutes. The cytocentrifuged scrape material technique was named SRCC. Smears were then prepared and stained with H&E, PAP, and MGG; H&E/PAP smears were fixed in isopropyl alcohol and MGG smears were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: All four cytology techniques were applied to the same 27 cases, so index-test arms are not independent. For SRCC, one case was nondiagnostic overall, and among 23 cases with histopathology, SRCC diagnosis was offered in 22 cases.

site_selection_index_test: Manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites.
technique: Patients underwent a complete clinical interview followed by conventional oral examination consisting of manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; based on clinical characteristics, the examiner classified lesions as benign or malignant.
positivity_threshold: Positive if the lesion was clinically classified/suspected as malignant by COE.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The COE examiner classified lesions in the absence of histological data.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information; patients had a complete clinical interview and classification was based on clinical characteristics.
comments_index_test: Same 35 patients/lesions were assessed by both unskilled and skilled dentists and also underwent VelScope; index-test arms are paired/non-independent.

site_selection_index_test: VelScope examination was applied to the clinically identified oral mucosal lesions after a complete clinical interview and conventional oral examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; lesions were classified as benign or malignant before Vel-E.
technique: The VelScope device was used at approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to visualize natural tissue fluorescence; the operating theatre was darkened if needed to reduce natural light to an acceptable level.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of loss of autofluorescence (LAF), the VelScope examination was defined positive.
calibration_of_assessors: No training/calibration was reported for the unskilled general dentist; the paper contrasts this examiner with the other dentist who had completed a 1-year oral medicine training program.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Index-test examiners performed VelScope examination in the absence of histological data, i.e. before knowing the reference standard result.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information; VelScope was performed on the basis of clinical information after clinical interview and conventional oral examination.
comments_index_test: Same 35 patients were assessed with VelScope by both the unskilled and skilled general dentists, so index-test arms are paired/non-independent. The u-GD arm represents an inexperienced examiner without the 1-year oral medicine training received by the comparator s-GD.

site_selection_index_test: Complete clinical oral examination including manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites.
technique: Patients underwent a complete clinical interview followed by COE, consisting of manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; based on clinical characteristics, the skilled GD classified lesions as benign or malignant.
positivity_threshold: Lesions classified as malignant/suspected malignant based on clinical characteristics found during COE.
calibration_of_assessors: The skilled general dentist had completed a 1-year training program in oral medicine at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The examiners performed the clinical classification and VelScope examination in the absence of histological data.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The s-GD was not blinded to clinical information; the examination was performed after a complete clinical interview and on the basis of clinical information.
comments_index_test: Same 35 patients/lesions were assessed by both the unskilled and skilled GDs and also underwent VelScope; COE s-GD results are therefore paired with other arms rather than independent.

site_selection_index_test: VelScope examination was performed on oral mucosal lesions after complete clinical interview and conventional oral examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; lesions were classified clinically and Vel-E was performed on the basis of clinical information.
technique: The VelScope device was used approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to visualize natural tissue fluorescence; the operating theatre was darkened if necessary to reduce ambient light to an acceptable level.
positivity_threshold: Vel-E was defined positive in the presence of loss of autofluorescence (LAF), where dysplastic tissue showed darker aspects compared with surrounding areas.
calibration_of_assessors: The skilled general dentist had completed a 1-year oral medicine training program before performing COE and VelScope examination.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The VelScope examiners performed Vel-E in the absence of histological data, i.e., blinded to the reference standard result at the time of the index test.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The examiner was not blinded to clinical information; Vel-E was performed on the basis of clinical information after complete clinical interview and clinical oral examination.
comments_index_test: Same 35 patients were examined by both u-GD and s-GD VelScope arms, so arm-level accuracy estimates are paired/non-independent. Also, biopsy incision margins were guided by Vel-E, which may affect reference-standard sampling.

index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's (Changsha) DNA Image Cytometer
site_selection_index_test: Oral mucosal lesions were sampled; incisional biopsies were performed at the same locations where brush samples were obtained.
specimen_collection: After mouth rinsing with water, the clinician gently scraped the oral mucosal lesion at least 10 times with a flexible cotton cytology brush; the brush head was stored in cell preservation solution and sent to the laboratory within 24 hours.
technique: Brush samples were processed using liquid-based thin-layer cell preparation, Feulgen staining, and scanning with the GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System DNA Image Cytometer. DNA quantitative analysis was performed only when at least 300 epithelial cell nuclei were present and normalized to normal epithelial nuclei; DNA content was expressed as a DNA index and used to classify nuclei into diploid, aneuploid, hyperdiploid, or tetraploid groups.
positivity_threshold: The oral specimen was classified as having abnormal DNA content if the aneuploid group had more than 3 nuclei (1% of at least 300 nuclei), or the hyperdiploid group had 5% of the total number of nuclei, or the tetraploid group had 10% of the total number of nuclei.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal DNA content by DI cell-count thresholds
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA image cytometry was performed blinded to the histological results.
comments_index_test: Authors noted a potential methodological limitation of this index-test arm: use of cotton brushes may have reduced accuracy because they may not obtain cells from the entire epithelial layer.

site_selection_index_test: The cytobrush biopsy was performed on the OPMD lesion before scalpel biopsy; the brush sample was taken from the whole lesion and the scalpel biopsy was taken from the same location as the brushing.
specimen_collection: Brush sample collected by brushing the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit before scalpel biopsy.
technique: Before scalpel biopsy, each patient underwent cytobrush biopsy at the same lesion location; the whole lesion was brushed using the MotiSavant liquid-based brush kit, and DNA content status was then analyzed using image cytometry according to the manufacturer's protocol.
positivity_threshold: At least 1 aneuploid cell with a DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: at least one aneuploid cell with DI ≥ 3.5
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analysts were blinded to histopathological results because DNA content analyses were completed before histopathological diagnoses.
comments_index_test: The DI ≥ 3.5 threshold was derived using ROC/maximum Youden index in the training set and then validated in the test set; diagnostic results are reported separately for training and test sets rather than as one combined estimate.

index_test_arm_label: Risk model (DNA-ICM with lateral/ventral tongue and non-homogenous lesions)
index_test_reagent_name: DNA-ICM (DI ≥ 3.5), lateral/ventral tongue, and non-homogenous lesions
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush sampling was applied to the OPMD lesion, brushing the whole lesion before scalpel biopsy; the risk model also categorized lesion site as lateral/ventral tongue versus other sites.
specimen_collection: Oral brushing specimen collected by cytobrush biopsy of the whole lesion using a liquid-based brush kit.
technique: Patients had clinical lesion features recorded, including lesion site and lesion type. Before biopsy, a cytobrush biopsy was taken from the same lesion location by brushing the whole lesion with the MotiSavant liquid-based brush kit. DNA content was then analyzed by DNA-ICM. The risk model summed scores for lateral/ventral tongue, non-homogenous lesion type, and DNA aneuploidy; a risk score ≥4 was used as the diagnostic cut-off.
positivity_threshold: Risk model positive when the risk score was ≥4.
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analysts were blinded to histopathological results; histopathology was completed after DNA content analysis.
comments_index_test: Combined risk model rather than DNA-ICM alone; it incorporates cytobrush DNA aneuploidy plus clinical lesion site and lesion type. Model was developed in the 608-patient training set and validated in the 202-patient test set, with the score cut-off optimized using the Youden index.

site_selection_index_test: The test was applied over the clinically assessed representative mucosal site for the oral white/red lesion.
technique: Patients rinsed with distilled water for 1 minute; 1% Rose Bengal solution was applied for 2 minutes over the clinically assessed site; patients then rinsed again with distilled water for 1 minute to remove excess dye; the stained lesion was examined intraorally and staining intensity was visually evaluated as mild, moderate, intense, or negative.
positivity_threshold: Positive staining was visually classified as mild positive, moderate positive, or intense positive; negative staining was classified separately.
comments_index_test: All patients received Rose Bengal staining, microbiopsy, and scalpel biopsy on the same lesion; index-test arms are paired within the same participants/lesions rather than independent groups.

site_selection_index_test: Microbiopsy was performed at the same clinically assessed site, specifically the intensely stained region after Rose Bengal staining.
specimen_collection: A 3 mm dermatological ring curette was used to scrape the intensely stained lesional area gently with the sharp edge of the curette until pinpoint mucosal bleeding occurred, to ensure basal layer sampling; multiple tissue fragments were obtained.
technique: After Rose Bengal staining, oral microbiopsy was performed at the same site using a 3 mm dermatological ring curette. The intensely stained lesional area was gently scraped with the curette’s sharp edge until pinpoint mucosal bleeding confirmed basal layer sampling. Multiple tissue fragments were processed, embedded, sectioned, stained with H&E, coded randomly, examined by light microscopy, and epithelial dysplasia was graded using Banoczy and Csiba criteria.
positivity_threshold: Histopathological indicators of epithelial dysplasia, described as cellular and architectural changes, graded using Banoczy and Csiba criteria.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The observer was blinded to the result of vital staining and scalpel biopsy.
comments_index_test: Microbiopsy was not an independent site-selection procedure: it was performed after Rose Bengal staining at the same site, specifically the intensely stained region. All patients received all three procedures on the same lesion, so index-test arms are paired/overlapping rather than independent.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: GOCCLES® scanning was applied to each clinically identified oral lesion compatible with OPMDs or OSCC after visual examination and recording of lesion location/characteristics.
technique: After visual examination, tissue was irradiated using an SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp at 440–480 nm and 1500 mW/cm² from 20 cm away. The irradiated tissue was then observed through the GOCCLES® device, and photographs were taken using the device kit mobile camera filter with a Xiaomi Redmi Note 9S smartphone.
positivity_threshold: Lesions showing fluorescence loss, visible as brown or dark green areas through the device, were classified as GOCCLES® positive. Lesions without visible dark areas, where all tissue appeared within the green spectrum, were classified as GOCCLES® negative.
calibration_of_assessors: All GOCCLES® and related procedures were performed by the same professional with specialized training in oral medicine; no additional calibration exercise was reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded/unclear scope: the paper reports lack of examiner blinding because the same professional performed all procedures, including biopsy site selection. This suggests the GOCCLES® examiner was not blinded to other clinical/procedural information, but the exact information available is not specified.
comments_index_test: GOCCLES® and toluidine blue were applied to the same 32 cases, so arms are not independent. The combined-method analysis used only the 18 cases with concordant GOCCLES® and TB results.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: TB staining was applied to the clinically identified oral lesions after visual examination and documentation of each lesion's location and characteristics.
technique: TB staining was performed following Mashberg (1983), but the paper does not describe the step-by-step staining procedure.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with intense blue staining were classified as positive for TB, while those with no staining or with only slight or diffuse staining were considered negative.
calibration_of_assessors: The same professional with specialized training in oral medicine performed the procedures; no specific calibration or standardization exercise was reported.
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR for blinding to the reference standard result; the paper states a general lack of examiner blinding but does not specifically state whether TB interpretation was blinded to histopathology.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The examiner was not blinded, although the paper does not specify exactly which clinical information was available; all procedures including biopsy site selection were performed by the same professional.
comments_index_test: All 32 cases appear to have received both GOCCLES® and toluidine blue, so this TB arm is not independent of the GOCCLES® arm. The TB procedural details are not described beyond stating that Mashberg's technique was followed.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: Index tests were applied to clinically identified oral lesions compatible with OPMDs or OSCC; each lesion was visually examined and documented before GOCCLES® scanning and TB staining.
technique: Both component tests were performed sequentially. For GOCCLES®, tissue was irradiated with a UV/blue light source from an SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp at 440–480 nm and 1500 mW/cm², applied 20 cm from the lesion; the tissue was observed through GOCCLES® and photographed. TB staining was then performed according to Mashberg’s technique.
positivity_threshold: Combined positive when both GOCCLES® and TB were positive: GOCCLES® positive was fluorescence loss visible as brown or dark green areas; TB positive was intense blue staining.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: both fluorescence loss and intense blue stain
calibration_of_assessors: All procedures were performed by the same professional with specialized training in oral medicine; no additional study-specific calibration was reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded or unclear; the authors state there was a lack of examiner blinding because the same professional performed all procedures, including biopsy site selection.
comments_index_test: Combined-arm analysis excluded discordant GOCCLES®/TB cases and included only 18 concordant cases out of 32, so the combined diagnostic estimates do not apply to all tested participants. The combined arm also overlaps with the individual GOCCLES® and TB arms.

site_selection_index_test: Samples were collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area.
specimen_collection: Samples from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area were collected using a cytology brush.
technique: The cytology-brush material was transferred onto a glass slide with care to minimize cell damage; conventional alcohol-fixed smears were then stained by the Papanicolaou method and interpreted by a cytopathologist.
positivity_threshold: “positive” indicated malignant cells present
comments_index_test: Paired multi-arm design: the same 60-patient cohort appears to have been evaluated by PAP staining, brush cytology VPAC staining, and oral gargle VPAC staining.

site_selection_index_test: Samples were taken from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area.
specimen_collection: Cells were collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area using a cytology brush and transferred onto a glass slide with care to minimize cell damage.
technique: Harvested brush cytology material on glass slides was fixed in 97% alcohol. TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) was added to cover the cell area, the slide was kept in the dark at 22°C for about 20 minutes, then rinsed with deionized water and air dried. DAPI was added, a coverslip placed, and the slide examined using a fluorescent microscope.
positivity_threshold: Cells showing TP4303 interaction with dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus were considered VPAC receptor positive/malignant; absence of VPAC receptor staining showed only the DAPI-bound nucleus in dark blue.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark orange TP4303 fluorescence around nucleus
comments_index_test: All three index-test approaches appear to have been evaluated in the same 60-patient cohort, so results across arms are not independent.

site_selection_index_test: Whole-mouth oral gargle sample; exfoliated cells shed into oral gargles were collected rather than applying the test to a specific lesion site.
specimen_collection: Patients gargled with 20 cc normal saline for a few minutes and spat the contents into a collecting cup; the fluid was centrifuged and the sediment placed on a glass slide.
technique: For oral gargle VPAC testing, the collected gargle fluid was centrifuged, sediment was transferred to a glass slide and fixed in 97% alcohol. The same VPAC staining protocol was then used: TP4303 solution was added to cover the cell area, the slide was kept in the dark at 22°C for about 20 minutes, rinsed with deionized water and air dried, DAPI was added, a coverslip placed, and the slide examined by fluorescent microscopy.
positivity_threshold: Cells were classified positive for VPAC receptors when TP4303 interaction produced dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus, indicating VPAC receptor molecules on the cell surface.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: VPAC-associated orange fluorescence around nucleus
comments_index_test: Same 60 patients appear to have undergone multiple index tests, including PAP staining, brush cytology VPAC staining, and oral gargle VPAC staining; arm results are therefore paired/non-independent.

site_selection_index_test: FV images were taken of the oral lesion; a lesion ROI was defined as the area of FVL, with a control ROI in normal mucosa at a distance away in the same oral sub-site.
technique: ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® were used randomly at the attending physician’s discretion. FV images were obtained and saved digitally; images were taken in a room made as dark as possible, with the irradiating light perpendicular to the lesion and an irradiation range of about 10 cm. Oral conditions and FV images were then compared subjectively, and FV images were also analyzed with ImageJ using lesion and control ROIs.
positivity_threshold: Positive case was defined as FVL; negative case was defined as only FVA or FVR, by two or more screenings using the surface plot as a reference.
comments_index_test: Retrospective study; ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® results are pooled, and the instrument used was chosen randomly/left to the attending physician rather than analyzed as separate arms.

site_selection_index_test: Methylene blue was applied to clinically suspected oral lesions selected after history and systematic oral examination; included lesions were non-healing ulcers or patches persisting for more than two weeks or unresponsive to treatment. The mucosa of the intended area was dried before dye application.
technique: Participants rinsed with solution B for 20 seconds, the intended mucosal area was dried with a triple syringe and gauze, solution A containing 1% methylene blue was applied, after a 20-second wait participants rinsed again with solution B for 20 seconds, and stain intensity was assessed by one observer. Cotton rolls with solution B were used to clear the stained surface when results were ambiguous.
positivity_threshold: Positive reaction was defined by local, stippled/stipules, concentrated blue stains or retained stain; wide and faint blue stains indicated a negative reaction.
comments_index_test: Biopsy site was selected from the area with highest methylene blue uptake, so the index test appears to have guided reference-standard sampling; this may affect diagnostic accuracy estimates.

site_selection_index_test: Oral mucosal lesions were first identified during conventional oral examination under white light as clinically suspicious OPMD or early SCC; these lesions were then photographed with IllumiScan®. For normal oral mucosa, ROIs were selected at sublingual mucosa, buccal mucosa, the transition from molar attached gingiva to buccal mucosa, and floor-of-mouth mucosa.
technique: Lesions were photographed under white light, then imaged with IllumiScan® in a dark room with constant irradiation brightness and an approximate 30 mm distance between the lens and lesion. Images were transferred to a computer and analysed in ImageJ: RGB components were separated, a green-component black-and-white image was created, an ROI was defined on the lesion area based on intraoral photographs/findings, FI was measured on a 0–255 scale, and average FI, SD, and CV were calculated.
positivity_threshold: ROC/Youden-derived thresholds were reported: average FI cut-off 98.5, SD cut-off 11.2, and CV cut-off 1.70. The main diagnostic threshold for distinguishing SCC was CV cut-off 1.70.
comments_index_test: IllumiScan® results were quantitatively post-processed rather than interpreted solely by visual fluorescence loss. Diagnostic cut-offs were ROC/Youden-derived within the study, not externally validated or clearly pre-specified. NOM controls were younger volunteers and were not biopsy-confirmed, while OML cases required biopsy confirmation.

site_selection_index_test: The entire clinically suspicious oral lesion was scraped; for multiple lesions, a different coverslip was used for each lesion to prevent crossover of cells.
specimen_collection: Cells were collected by vigorously scraping the entire lesion with a coverslip, then spreading the harvested cells onto glass slides.
technique: Two glass slides were prepared per lesion. After recording patient details and smear site on the slide, excess saliva was removed with gauze. The entire lesion was scraped with a coverslip, the harvested cells were spread onto a glass slide, and the slide was immediately placed in a Koplin jar containing 80% alcohol fixative. The same procedure was repeated for a second smear from the same lesion; different coverslips were used for multiple lesions.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: Diagnostic accuracy denominators are unclear. The Results section reports inconsistent patient counts in the age/sex table versus text, and the paper does not provide a clear 2×2 table or explicit number of patients/lesions analyzed for exfoliative cytology.

site_selection_index_test: Biopsy sediment cytology was applied to fixatives from biopsied oral lesions with provisional diagnoses of oral pre-malignant or malignant lesions; no separate intra-oral site-selection procedure for the cytology test was described.
specimen_collection: Specimen consisted of leftover formalin from biopsy specimen bottles after the biopsy specimens were transferred to fresh fixative; the sediment from this fixative was used for cytology.
technique: The original specimen-bottle fixative was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes; supernatant was discarded; sediments were washed twice in normal saline; smears were prepared on albumen-coated slides, fixed in 95% ethanol with 3% glacial acetic acid Biofix spray, stained with Papanicolaou stain, and analyzed by two observers.
positivity_threshold: Cytology was classified by Shafer’s classes: Class I normal, Class II atypia, Class III intermediate, Class IV suggestive of cancer, Class V positive for cancer. Reporting was negative as Class I, positive for OPMDs as Class II and III, and positive for oral malignant lesions as Class IV and V.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: Shafer Class II/III for OPMD or Class IV/V for malignancy
comments_index_test: Index test used biopsy specimen fixative sediment, so the cytology test depended on a biopsy specimen already being collected rather than being a direct in-vivo screening test.

index_test_reagent_name: handheld VELscope (C Ultra by Technomax Corporation, Pune, Maharashtra)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious oral lesions; for each lesion, autofluorescence examination by VELscope was carried out after conventional oral examination.
technique: After conventional oral examination, autofluorescence visualization was performed using a handheld VELscope; findings were categorized as loss of fluorescence or retained/no loss of fluorescence according to the manufacturer's literature.
positivity_threshold: Loss of fluorescence was categorized as the positive/suspicious AFV finding; retained or no loss of fluorescence was categorized as negative.
comments_index_test: NA

site_selection_index_test: All study participants with suspicious OPMDs identified at baseline underwent another oral examination with OralID®; details regarding all OPMDs visible with fluorescent light were recorded.
technique: After conventional oral examination, suspicious OPMDs were re-examined by the same clinician using OralID®, a handheld light emitting visible blue light at 435–460 nm directly into the oral cavity so the clinician could view tissue fluorescence and record fluorescent-light findings.
positivity_threshold: Oral lesions illuminating bright green or white green were recorded as no OPMDs; those with lack of fluorescence or dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas, were recorded as OPMDs.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss or dark areas
blinding_index_test_examiner: The OralID® examiner was not blinded to the preceding conventional examination findings because the same clinician performed both examinations; the authors note this could introduce reporting bias.
comments_index_test: Same dentist performed both conventional and fluorescence examinations, creating potential reporting bias. The paper states lesions were the unit of analysis, but the diagnostic table and results refer to 44 participants and sum to 44 analyzed units, so patient/lesion unit is somewhat ambiguous.

site_selection_index_test: Velscope was applied to oral tissues/lesions in patients clinically diagnosed with OPMDs; the paper does not describe a systematic site-selection protocol beyond examination of the oral tissues before biopsy.
technique: Patients underwent Velscope examination before incisional biopsy in a dark room while wearing special glasses from the Velscope kit. Blue light at 400–460 nm was directed onto the oral tissues, and emitted fluorescence was visually assessed; loss of autofluorescence appeared as dark areas suggesting dysplasia.
positivity_threshold: Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
comments_index_test: Results text contains an apparent inconsistency/typographical error stating Velscope identified 51 participants as positive, but the study sample and Table 3 show 40 participants total with 31 Velscope-positive and 9 Velscope-negative results.

site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity was visually inspected.
technique: Conventional visual oral examination was performed by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons; leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possible oral cancer were classified as abnormal findings.
positivity_threshold: The VOE assessment of leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possibly oral cancer were identified as abnormal findings.
comments_index_test: VOE was evaluated in the same 201-patient cohort that also received ZNF582 methylation testing and histopathologic verification; the paper reports adjusted logistic prediction models for VOE, MET, triage, and co-testing rather than a simple standalone VOE 2x2 diagnostic table.

site_selection_index_test: Oral exfoliated cell specimens were collected from the mucosal lesion of each patient.
specimen_collection: Oral epithelial cells were collected from the oral mucosal lesion using an oral swab/foam brush and preserved in an Epigene Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube.
technique: Oral epithelial cells were collected with a foam brush and preserved; genomic DNA was extracted using the Epigene Nucleic Acid Extraction kit. Extracted DNA was quantified, bisulfite converted, and assayed for ZNF582 methylation using the Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit by quantitative methylation-specific PCR with TaqMan technology on a LightCycler LC480. COL2A was used as an internal reference/validity indicator, and methylation status was qualitatively determined according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: The exact ZNF582 methylation positivity cutoff is not reported; results were classified qualitatively according to manufacturer instructions. The commercial kit manufacturer was also the study funder, and several authors were employees of iStat Biomedical.

index_test_reagent_name: abnormal VOE findings and methylation positivity
site_selection_index_test: Conventional VOE was performed by experienced oral maxillofacial surgeons; for the methylation component, oral exfoliated cells were collected from the mucosal lesion.
specimen_collection: Oral exfoliated epithelial cells were collected from the mucosal lesion by oral swab/foam brush and preserved in an “Epigene” Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube.
technique: Patients first underwent conventional VOE by experienced OMS. Oral exfoliated epithelial cells were then collected from the mucosal lesion using a foam brush, preserved in an Epigene tube, and genomic DNA was extracted. DNA concentration was quantified, bisulfite conversion was performed, and ZNF582 methylation was determined using the Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit by quantitative methylation-specific PCR with TaqMan technology on a LightCycler LC480, using COL2A as internal reference/validity indicator. The triage model classified patients using an indicator requiring both abnormal VOE findings and methylation positivity.
positivity_threshold: Positive in the triage model required both abnormal VOE findings and ZNF582 methylation positivity. Abnormal VOE findings included leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possible oral cancer; the exact methylation Cp cutoff was not reported beyond qualitative determination according to manufacturer instructions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal VOE and methylation positivity
comments_index_test: The triage model appears to be a modeled sequential strategy rather than a purely prospective sequential workflow: all 201 patients underwent both VOE and ZNF582 methylation testing, and the triage indicator was then defined as abnormal VOE plus methylation positivity.

site_selection_index_test: VOE involved examination of the oral cavity, and the ZNF582 methylation specimen was collected from the mucosal lesion after physical examination.
specimen_collection: Oral exfoliated epithelial cells were collected from the mucosal lesion by oral swab/foam brush and preserved in an Epigene Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube.
technique: Combined co-testing consisted of conventional VOE by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons plus ZNF582 methylation testing. For the methylation assay, oral epithelial cells were collected with a foam brush, genomic DNA was extracted, quantified, bisulfite converted, and tested for ZNF582 methylation by quantitative methylation-specific PCR using TaqMan technology on a LightCycler LC480; results were qualitatively determined according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
positivity_threshold: NR for a single co-testing positivity threshold. The paper describes abnormal VOE categories and qualitative ZNF582 methylation results, but the co-testing arm was modeled by adding both VOE and methylation marker to the reference logistic model rather than by a prespecified binary positivity rule.
comments_index_test: Co-testing was analyzed as a multivariable logistic regression/ROC model including both VOE and methylation marker, adjusted for age, sex, and betel nut chewing, not as a clearly prespecified standalone binary diagnostic test. All patients appear to have received both component tests.

site_selection_index_test: Lesional and perilesional tissue of clinically suspicious oral lesions was assessed with the VELscope after routine oral examination.
technique: Direct visual examination was performed using the VELscope/VELscopeVX handpiece. Lesional and perilesional tissues were viewed through the handpiece and assessed for visual fluorescence retention or visual fluorescence loss; findings were documented and digital photographs were acquired through the handpiece using an iPod 5 camera with an adapter.
positivity_threshold: Visual fluorescence loss (VFL) was classified as positive; visual fluorescence retention (VFR) was classified as negative.
comments_index_test: NA
