index_test_reagent_name: device for direct fluorescence visualization (direct FV)
site_selection_index_test: The oral cavity was viewed with direct FV after a white-light oral mucosal assessment to identify new or altered clinical lesions, with particular attention to sites of previous lesions/prior oral SCC.
technique: After room lights were turned off, clinicians viewed the oral cavity directly using the direct FV handheld device. The device projected blue excitation light onto the oral mucosa via coaxial excitation/emission pathways; green-red tissue fluorescence was viewed through the handheld unit. Normal mucosa appeared pale green, while areas with reduced fluorescence were identified visually.
positivity_threshold: Tissue showing a distinct reduction in the normal pale green fluorescence and appearing dark green to black was classified as fluorescence visualization loss (FVL), i.e., positive for abnormality.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The paper does not explicitly state blinding to clinical information. The sequence suggests the clinicians had clinical information/white-light findings before direct FV, because each visit first involved white-light assessment and biopsy decisions were based on patient history, clinical appearance, and toluidine blue staining, not on direct FV.
comments_index_test: Lesion/site-level analysis of 50 biopsies from 44 high-risk follow-up patients with prior biopsy-confirmed oral dysplasia or SCC; biopsy decisions were based on standard clinical features and toluidine blue, not on direct FV.

site_selection_index_test: FNAC was performed after localizing the oral lesion/pathological site.
specimen_collection: After localizing the lesion, FNAC specimen was collected using a 23–24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe; aspirated material was spread on clean numbered slides.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with water before sample collection. FNAC was performed by a cytopathologist with the patient supine or sitting with head support. After lesion localization, a 23–24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable syringe was used; aspirated material was spread on clean numbered slides. Wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol for Papanicolaou stain, and air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky/Diff-Quik.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: FNAC and scrape cytology appear to have been performed in the same patient cohort, but reported diagnostic accuracy tables describe 'cytology' overall rather than clearly separating FNAC-specific results from scrape cytology results.

site_selection_index_test: Scrape cytology was performed from pathological sites, frequently mucosal lesions, and other representative oral sites.
specimen_collection: Scrape smears were collected using a wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological/mucosal oral sites after patients washed the oral cavity with water.
technique: Patients washed the oral cavity with water; scrape cytology samples were collected by a cytopathologist using a wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological/mucosal sites; wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol for Papanicolaou staining and air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky/Diff-Quik stain.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: Scrape cytology is described as a study procedure, but some results and discussion refer broadly to cytology or to scrape cytology and aspiration cytology together, so scrape-specific diagnostic results may not always be clearly separable from FNAC.

site_selection_index_test: Participants with oral mucosal lesions were screened, and the identified lesions were subjected to DrOroscope examination.
technique: DrOroscope examination used blue-light autofluorescence imaging: normal tissue reflects green fluorescence, abnormal tissue shows loss of fluorescence and appears dark; images were captured with the device sensor and analyzed using AI-based software algorithms, after which lesions were categorized as variable, borderline, or dysplasia/severe.
positivity_threshold: Loss of fluorescence on blue-light exposure, with abnormal tissues appearing dark; DrOroscope categorized lesions into variable, borderline, and severe/dysplasia categories after image analysis.
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner was trained in operating DrOroscope and interpreting its results.
comments_index_test: Counts are reported at the participant/case level only; separate lesion-level denominators are not explicitly stated. The study also does not report blinding of the DrOroscope examiner/interpreter.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious OPMD lesions/areas were examined with VELscope; biopsy sites were later selected based on lesions positive by VELscope and/or vital stains.
technique: VELscope examination was performed by another investigator from approximately 3–4 inches away; tissue fluorescence was recorded as fluorescence retention or loss, and fluorescence photographs were documented.
positivity_threshold: Fluorescence loss was considered abnormal/positive for dysplasia: normal oral mucosa retains pale green fluorescence, while areas with dysplasia, inflammation, or increased vascularization lose fluorescence and appear dark.
comments_index_test: All index-test arms appear to have been applied to the same 30 patients, so VELscope and vital stain arms are overlapping rather than independent.

site_selection_index_test: Vital stains, including methylene blue, were applied on the suspicious area after VELscope examination.
technique: After VELscope examination and photographic documentation, methylene blue was applied as one of the vital stains on the suspicious area; stain uptake was assessed and photographs were documented.
positivity_threshold: Deep blue stains, which were local, stippled and patchy were considered to be positive, whereas faint blue stains, which were wide, shallow & could be easily washable, were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: deep local stippled or patchy blue stain retention
comments_index_test: The same 30 participants appear to have received all four index tests, so index-test arms are paired/non-independent rather than separate patient groups.

site_selection_index_test: Vital staining with toluidine blue was applied on the suspicious area of clinically diagnosed OPMD lesions.
technique: After VELscope examination and photographic documentation, toluidine blue vital staining was performed on the suspicious area; stain uptake was recorded photographically and interpreted as positive or negative for dysplasia.
positivity_threshold: Uptake of stain was considered positive for dysplasia; no uptake or light uptake of staining was considered negative.
comments_index_test: Same 30 patients appear to have received all index tests in a paired multi-arm design; biopsy site selection may have been influenced by positive VELscope/vital stain findings, although biopsy was stated to be performed irrespective of VELscope or staining findings.

site_selection_index_test: Lugol's iodine was applied as a vital stain to the clinically suspicious oral area/lesion.
technique: The paper reports only that Lugol's iodine was applied as one of the vital stains to the suspicious area after VELscope examination, with photographs documented and stain response assessed; no detailed Lugol-specific application steps, dwell time, or rinsing protocol were reported.
positivity_threshold: For vital stains generally, the Methods state that uptake of stain was considered positive for dysplasia and no/light uptake was negative; however, the Lugol's iodine discussion states that malignant tissues remain unstained whereas normal epithelium stains brown or black.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: unstained area / lack of iodine staining
comments_index_test: All four index tests appear to have been applied to the same 30 patients, so arms are paired/non-independent. Lugol's iodine positivity criterion is ambiguously reported: Methods gives a shared vital-stain rule of stain uptake = positive, but the Lugol discussion describes dysplastic/malignant tissue as remaining unstained.

index_test_arm_label: Liquid-based brush biopsy (Cytobrush GT nylon brush)
site_selection_index_test: Conspicuous, clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa were sampled with the Cytobrush GT nylon brush.
specimen_collection: At least five brush smears were taken per lesion with the nylon brush; the brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion, rotated at least ten times, and then washed thoroughly into a SurePath preservation vial.
technique: Liquid-based cytology using the Cytobrush GT nylon brush: at least five brush smears per lesion were obtained, with the brush head placed tangentially to the lesion and rotated at least ten times; the brush head was washed thoroughly in the SurePath preservation vial. Samples were shipped to an experienced pathologist, processed according to the SurePath protocol, transferred to glass slides, stained with Papanicolaou, and evaluated using the German classification for extragenital cytology.
positivity_threshold: Cytological results categorized as 'doubtful', 'suspicious' or 'positive' were considered tumour cell positive; only 'negative' was considered tumour cell negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful, suspicious, or positive cytology
comments_index_test: The nylon-brush arm was a historical cohort from 2009–2012 and used five pooled brush smears per lesion, whereas the comparator rigid-brush arm was from 2012–2018 and used one obtainment; this non-concurrent design and different sampling intensity may affect comparisons between arms.

index_test_arm_label: Liquid-based brush biopsy (Orcellex Brush rigid brush)
site_selection_index_test: Conspicuous, clearly visible oral lesions showing variation from normal healthy mucosa were sampled; for the rigid brush, the Orcellex Brush was used for sampling these oral lesions.
specimen_collection: One brush-biopsy specimen was obtained using the rigid brush: the brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion, rotated at least ten times, and then washed thoroughly into the preservation vial.
technique: Liquid-based brush biopsy using the Orcellex rigid brush: one obtainment was performed routinely; the brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times, then washed thoroughly in a SurePath preservation vial. Samples were shipped to an experienced pathologist, processed according to the SurePath protocol, transferred to glass slides, stained by Papanicolaou, and evaluated using the German classification for extragenital cytology.
positivity_threshold: Cytological results categorized as 'doubtful', 'suspicious' or 'positive' were considered tumour cell positive; only 'negative' was considered tumour cell negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful, suspicious, or positive cytology
comments_index_test: Rigid brush arm was a retrospective/consecutive temporal cohort rather than a randomized concurrent arm: Orcellex was used from June 2012 to February 2018, after the nylon-brush cohort. Only one rigid-brush obtainment was taken, whereas five nylon-brush smears were taken and pooled, so arm comparisons are confounded by both time period and sampling procedure.

site_selection_index_test: Oral brush cytology was applied to clinically visible oral mucosal lesions that varied from normal healthy mucosa; specimen collection sites included the tongue, gingiva, floor of the mouth, buccal mucosa, palate, and lips.
specimen_collection: Cell samples were collected from the oral lesion using an Orcellex® Brush; after twisting the brush ten times, the brush head was placed directly into the alcohol-based BD SurePath™ collection vial.
technique: BD SurePath™ liquid-based cytology was performed. Cells were collected with an Orcellex® Brush by twisting the brush ten times, then the brush head was transferred into an alcohol-based BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to the laboratory. The cells were stained with Papanicolaou stain according to the standard procedure. Slides were checked for adequacy and independently assessed by at least two oral pathology diagnostic experts, with discrepancies resolved by consensus.
positivity_threshold: For diagnostic-accuracy analysis, cytology was classified as negative if the cytological diagnosis was negative, and positive if the cytological diagnosis was doubtful or positive. A “positive” diagnosis meant malignant cells were observed; “doubtful” meant malignant cells were suspected but not confirmed.
comments_index_test: Retrospective single-center study. Diagnostic-accuracy analysis appears to exclude 2 inadequate cytology samples: 653 received cytology, but the 2×2 table includes 436 cytology-negative plus 215 cytology-positive/doubtful patients, i.e. 651 analyzed. Doubtful cytology was treated as test-positive.

index_test_arm_label: Oral colposcopy using Reid's Colposcopic Index (RCI)
index_test_reagent_name: Acetic acid solution (5%) and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: The colposcopic examination was applied to the clinically suspected oral lesion; acetic acid and Lugol's solution were applied "to the lesion." Biopsy afterward was taken from the most suspicious area.
technique: After wiping the oral mucosa with saline, the examiner viewed vascular patterns using the green filter at high magnification (≥×30). Then 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion for about 60 seconds and aceto-whitening was assessed at low magnification (≤×20). Lugol's solution was then applied to assess iodine uptake at low magnification. The findings were scored using Reid's Colposcopic Index.
positivity_threshold: The cutoff value to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions was 5 according to the RCI.
comments_index_test: The RCI and Swede scoring system arms are not independent tests on separate populations; both scoring systems were applied to the same colposcopic examinations/cases.

index_test_arm_label: Oral colposcopy using Swede scoring system
index_test_reagent_name: Acetic acid solution (5%) and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected OPMD lesions were examined; the colposcopic reagents were applied to the lesion.
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, vascular patterns were viewed using the green filter at high magnification (≥×30). Then 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion for about 60 seconds and aceto-whitening was assessed at low magnification (≤×20). Then Lugol's solution was applied to assess iodine uptake at low magnification (≤×20).
positivity_threshold: The cutoff value to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions was 8 according to the Swede scoring system.
comments_index_test: Same colposcopic examination was interpreted using two scoring systems (Swede and RCI), so arms are not independent tests on separate patients. Two of 25 patients were missed for biopsy; diagnostic accuracy appears based on 23 cases with histopathology.

site_selection_index_test: All patients underwent the usual routine clinical examination of the oral cavity according to the standard protocol, with Roed-Petersen topographical recording of findings/suspect regions.
technique: White-light clinical assessment was performed first. The same experienced maxillofacial surgeon carried out the usual routine clinical examination according to the standard protocol and completed the Roed-Petersen protocol.
positivity_threshold: CA was positive when a suspect lesion was seen.
comments_index_test: Biopsy verification was conditional rather than universal: biopsy was performed only when a lesion was suspect on clinical or VELscope assessment and the examining surgeon judged biopsy necessary. This may affect interpretation of diagnostic accuracy for the conventional clinical examination arm.

site_selection_index_test: The oral cavity was examined in all patients after routine clinical examination; every suspect region was marked according to the Roed-Petersen protocol.
technique: All patients first underwent the usual routine clinical examination according to the standard protocol, with completion of the Roed-Petersen protocol. They then underwent VELscope examination of the oral cavity in a separate room with dimmed lights; patients and examiner wore safety goggles, suspect regions were marked, and additional diascopy was performed to detect inflammation. Biopsy was considered if either the clinical or VELscope assessment was suspect.
positivity_threshold: Clinical examination was positive when a suspect lesion was seen; VELscope/autofluorescence was positive when loss of fluorescence was observed.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: suspect lesion or fluorescence loss
comments_index_test: All 195 patients received both clinical examination and VELscope assessment, but biopsy was performed only in patients with suspect lesions, and the decision to biopsy was made by the examining surgeon using clinical aspects including inflammation; this may introduce partial verification/work-up bias for diagnostic accuracy estimates.

site_selection_index_test: Velscope examination was applied after conventional oral examination to selected high-risk subjects with suspicious oral mucosal lesions; the lesions documented during COE and Velscope examination were evaluated.
technique: Conventional oral examination was followed by autofluorescence examination using the Velscope. Lesions were interpreted by their autofluorescence appearance: greenish fluorescence indicated normal/healthy mucosa, while dark/brown fluorescence or complete fluorescence visualization loss was considered suggestive of dysplastic/malignant change; lesions with retained fluorescence or non-complete FVL patterns were grouped as FVR for analysis.
positivity_threshold: Dark/brownish fluorescence or complete fluorescence visualization loss (FVL) was considered positive; lesions were rated malignant or dysplastic only when there was complete FVL.
calibration_of_assessors: Velscope examination was reported as performed by a dental surgeon/trained field investigator, but no detailed calibration or standardization procedure was described.
comments_index_test: The paper alternates between patient-level and lesion-level wording; it reports 250 patients/subjects and 250 lesions, and the diagnostic 2×2 table is lesion-based. Velscope was performed after COE, and the detailed device operating protocol was not reported.

site_selection_index_test: Conventional oral examination was applied to the selected subjects with suspicious oral mucosal lesions; all lesions documented during COE were later reviewed/correlated.
technique: The conventional oral examination was performed by trained field investigators under white operatory light at CHCs and PHCs, and a provisional clinical diagnosis was recorded.
positivity_threshold: NR
calibration_of_assessors: Conventional oral examination was performed by trained field investigators; no further calibration or standardization procedure was reported.
comments_index_test: White Light Examination was performed in the same 250 participants before VELscope. Twelve WLE cases were categorized as 'No Result' and excluded from the WLE 2×2 diagnostic table, leaving 238 analyzed for WLE accuracy.
